newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks weak in morning, hurt by Japan/property.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks weak in morning, hurt by Japan/property.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks edged lower in Tuesday morning trade, affected by another slide in Japanese shares and continued weakness in the local property sector.
The Hang Seng Index was down 41.73 points, or 0.31 percent, at 13,247.48. Turnover was HK$2.35 billion after the first 45 minutes of trade.

"There is no reason why the market should have gone roaring up today. It had quite a good rise yesterday and there are no reasons to do an encore today," said Howard Gorges, director at South China Brokerage.
The blue-chip index rose 97.71 points on Monday.
Analysts said Tuesday's tumble in Japanese shares was dampening sentiment. The Nikkei 225 average closed the morning session down 446.50 points, or 2.46 percent, at 17,672.29.
"If people want to be cautious they will cast a wary eye over Japan," said Gorges.

Rory McAllister at HSBC James Capel said fresh economic data due to be released in the United States this week were also keeping some investors sidelined. "The performance on the Street was not that tremendous," he added.
The Dow industrials rose 5.39 points on Monday to 6,709.18 and the U.S. long bond slipped 2/32 to yield 6.85 percent.
"I think the market will be going just sideways in the near term. We have more economic data to come out of the States and a bond market that is still under pressure," said Gorges.
Property stocks remained weak, hurt by continued uncertainty surrounding possible government measures to curb property speculation.
Cheung Kong was down HK$0.25 at HK$71.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties shed HK$0.25 to HK$90.50.
Shares in Henderson Land were unchanged at HK$72.00 after the company said it planned to offer 30 million shares in a proposed secondary listing on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
"From Henderson Land's point of view it is a good thing -- they will get some cash and it does not appear to be a call on the market in Hong Kong," said Gorges.
Shares in China Travel International rose HK$0.05 to HK$3.825. The company said it would issue 700 million new shares to its parent China Travel Service at HK$3.60 per share.
"I think at the moment the red chips are really getting positive treatment," said Gorges. "Some of them are very speculative but China Travel is a company that has got good fundamentals."
